answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-weighted attestation groves: to join a grove, each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verified work over time. A newcomer starts in the orchard of unproven identities, where its attestations carry near-zero weight. Trust grows as a delta between proven output and claimed output — consistent, checkable work raises weight, while detected fakery slashes the deposit and burns the identity. Attackers must therefore pay real capital and sustained compute per fake identity, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
